sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 20 students, 8 preferred pizza. Based on this sample, about how many of the 200 students in the school would you expect to prefer pizza?

steps: Find the sample proportion: 8 out of 20 preferred pizza.
Scale up to the population: the school is 200 ÷ 20 = 10 times the sample size.

items.prompt: Five random samples of the same population produced these mean scores: 72, 75, 68, 74, 71. What is the range of these sample estimates?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A population has 259 commuters on a train line. Student A takes a random sample of 17. Student B takes a random sample of 50. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?
choices: Student B's sample of 50, because larger random samples tend to produce more consistent, accurate estimates.
Student A's sample of 17, because smaller samples are easier to analyze.
Both are equally likely to be accurate, because both are random.
Neither sample is reliable unless it includes the entire population.

items.prompt: A student surveys 11 shoppers at a grocery store using a simple random sample and records the results. Is it valid to generalize this result to all 132 shoppers at a grocery store?
choices: Yes, because the sample size is large enough regardless of how it was chosen.
Yes, because the sample was selected randomly, so it is likely representative of the population.
No, because the sample was not randomly selected, so it may not represent the population.
No, because samples can never be generalized to a population.

items.prompt: A sample of 6 values is: 46, 38, 38, 51, 44, 39. What is the median of this data set?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A data set has 4 values: 17, 15, 16, 16. What is the new mean if an outlier of 45 is added to the data set, making 5 values in all?
A data set is: 18, 18, 25, 19, 25, with a mean of 21. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of this data set?
Two data sets have means of 57 and 74. Their mean absolute deviation (MAD) is 8. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.
choices: 4 1/4 times the MAD
8 times the MAD
2 1/8 times the MAD
3 1/8 times the MAD

items.prompt: Sample A: 47, 25, 43, 28, 37, 24. Sample B: 71, 50, 69, 65, 51, 36. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
choices: Both samples have the same mean.
Sample B, with a mean of 57 compared to 34.
Sample A, with a mean of 34 compared to 57.
Sample B, with a mean of 34 compared to 57.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Sample A: 35, 29, 44, 38, 24. Sample B: 30, 30, 34, 31, 33. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Sample B, with a range of 20 compared to 4.
Sample A, with a range of 20 compared to 4.
Sample B, with a range of 4 compared to 20.
Both samples have the same range.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 346 visitors to a science museum. She randomly selects 19 of them to survey. What is the sample in this situation?
choices: Only the first 19 visitors to a science museum on a list
The researcher's own estimate
All 346 visitors to a science museum
The 19 randomly selected visitors to a science museum
